novelty_flags.label: literature_checklist entry Ponomarev2024
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited April 2024 paper characterizes a smallest nonredundant Artstein-inequality collection for broad set-valued-prediction models; it does not make the checklist's stated total-order-specific finite-core claim.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 2--4 and Appendix A, especially lines 29--43, 61--67, 103--110, and 177--194 of the arXiv HTML
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes consistency, positivity, strong sequential exchangeability, and FFRCISTG; proves sharp binary endpoints; and states that its lower and upper CDF envelope bounds are jointly attainable. Appendix A couples incompatible action subtrees to attain endpoint constructions.
For a dynamic regime, the FFRCISTG model gives SWIG factorization and dynamic modularity, conditional on the relevant conditional laws being well-defined.
The article characterizes distributions of random-set selections through capacity-type inequalities and establishes convex-compact/continuity properties.

source_verification_receipts.version: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 73(2), 1976, pp. 286--288
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For variables with an arbitrary common marginal, the paper defines maximal dependence by simultaneous attainment of the extremal maximum survival function.
The paper formalizes categorical structural-causal marginal compatibility using response functions and shows that marginal information restricts compatible joint SCMs.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 39(2), 2021, pp. 532--546
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives a sharp random-set/transport method for continuous functionals of joint potential-outcome distributions and notes computational considerations.
The paper characterizes scalar sharp identified-set endpoints by optimal transport, and its dual sample analogues are root-n consistent with weak convergence under stated conditions.
The article gives sharp ordinal benefit bounds and documents boundary/atom-driven nonregularity, including failure of ordinary bootstrap procedures in relevant cases.

The article develops sharp bounds and inference for distributions of binary-treatment effects, including covariate-available settings; it is the direct static distributional precursor omitted from the proposal map.

The paper characterizes the smallest collection of nonredundant Artstein inequalities sufficient for sharpness and provides an algorithm across set-valued-prediction applications; the abstract does not state a total-order-specific finite-core result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Fan and Park (2010) to the bibliography and compare its static sharp distributional bounds explicitly with the dynamic oracle-max target; state the first step where the SMART tree changes their coupling problem.

Replace the Ponomarev checklist description with its actual minimal-nonredundant-inequalities result, then explain precisely why the proposed local capacity system is smaller or structurally different.

State the projection theorem universally over observed laws P with completions Q in F(P), reserving consistency, exchangeability, factorization, and modularity for Q rather than informally attributing them to P.

For a higher-tier path, add a strict comparison theorem against at least two named whole-law or transport comparators, showing an observable regime in which the tree-diagonal formulation is strictly more informative or exponentially smaller than their formulations.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature map and checklist, retain the projection-and-lift question as the field-tier kernel, then advance to Stage 0 only after the Fan--Park and Ponomarev comparisons are corrected.
